assembly_instructions: 1) Start from the FPGA PCB substrate (14x9 m floorplan) and overlay the silicon-die outline plate that bounds the placed-and-routed logic, then scribe three thin floorplan partition lines dividing the die into memory, butterfly-array and reduction/control zones; on the -X edge seat the host interface: a PCIe x16 gold-finger edge connector feeding a host DMA/PCIe controller block, the boundary where coefficient vectors enter and transformed results leave. 2) Drive the controller into the forward-NTT input FIFO and natural-order output FIFO, then mount the eight interleaved BRAM banks along the left edge at 1.1 m pitch between them. 3) Drop the conflict-free crossbar network as a vertical spine just inboard of the banks, and place the inverse-NTT N^-1 scaling unit on its output side. 4) Build the open butterfly-array frame: lay a thin floor across the array, then bolt the two longitudinal steel rails and the mid cross-brace so the chassis stays open from above; populate the eight parallel radix-2 butterfly lanes (one per BRAM bank) by wiring each DSP modular multiplier into its symmetric modular adder (dark anodized) and subtractor (brushed steel), then both into the pipeline register; finally seat the four carbon-fiber radix-4 fusion yokes in the open gap between the multiplier and add/sub columns, each binding a lane-pair (0-1, 2-3, 4-5, 6-7) into one fused 4-input radix-4 butterfly unit so the eight radix-2 lanes reconfigure into four radix-4 BUs. 5) Place the shared modular-reduction stage to the right as two distinct members: first the cylindrical Barrett q-multiplier spanning all eight lanes, then the boxy shift/subtract+correction member abutting it, wired from every pipeline register. 6) Route the operand-return bus from the reduction member back over the array to the crossbar (grounded by a standoff post onto the reduction member), and route the operand-read bus from the crossbar east into the multiplier column (grounded by its own standoff onto the array frame), keeping the read, return and twiddle channels on three separate heights; cap each with a direction arrow so the read/twiddle/return dataflow triad is fully visible and the conflict-free read-modify-write loop is closed. 7) On the right, install the twiddle-factor ROM and route a brass broadcast feeder west to the elevated rail spanning the multiplier column (grounded by a standoff onto the array frame) so one fetched factor fans out to all eight multipliers; then add the address-generation unit, the radix-2/4 config selector, the schedule/FSM controller and the clock PLL. 8) For inspection, lift one fused radix-4 butterfly unit onto two riser posts into an exploded view above the array (three twiddle multipliers W1/W2/W3 -> constant j-rotator -> y0..y3 add/sub tree -> four-output register), offset toward the +Z half so it clears the central lanes in plan view; add two +X dataflow arrows (mult->add/sub, add/sub->register) on the exploded unit and a thin carbon-fiber fusion-callout strut from the lanes-6/7 yoke up to the exploded baseplate so the W1->W2->W3->j-rotator->add/sub->register order and the represented fused unit are unambiguous, and clamp the ten-fin exploded aluminum heatsink high onto its riser stub well above the die so the datapath below stays visible.

params.modulus_q_note: Source gives only '14-bit NTT-friendly prime'; reproduction fixes q=12289=3*2^12+1, the canonical 14-bit prime with 2048 | (q-1) so 2N-th roots of unity exist for a 1024-point transform. No other modulus is recoverable from the source — there is no distinct 'paper benchmark modulus' to substitute.
params.transform_flavor: Unstated in source; PQC/HE context implies negacyclic (psi = 2N=2048-th primitive root, omega = psi^2 the N-th root). Cyclic is the degenerate fallback the earlier functional impls used and is a likely mismatch.
params.twiddle_root_constraints: psi^2048 ≡ 1 and psi^1024 ≡ -1 (mod q); omega = psi^2; any generator satisfying these is a valid reproduction choice.

spec.notes:
Authoritative claims from CFNTT, TCHES 2022 issue 1, pp.94-126 (Chen et al., Tsinghua). The exact modulus q is given in the source only as a 14-bit NTT-friendly prime; the 1024-pt benchmark uses a 14-bit q. Verification auto-selects the SMT backend because this is a digital/compute design (NTT datapath), not a mechanical machine.
[src] q=12289, N=1024, coeff=14b, psi=1945 (negacyclic order 2048), omega=10302, Ninv=12277 from CFNTT (TCHES 2022). [calc] psi=1945=11^6 mod 12289; omega=10302=1945^2 mod 12289; Ninv=12277=1024^-1 mod 12289 (1024*12277=1+1023*12289); barrett_mu=21843=floor(2^28/12289), barrett_k=28 (q^2=151019521<2^28). [conv] generator g=11 (yields the source's psi) treated as reproduction-transcribed, not independently stated. [src] pipeline latency 9 cycles/lane = mult 3 + add/sub 1 + Barrett 4 + reg 1 (replaces prior 'functional-model/ignored' default). [src->calc] OP-COUNT RECONCILIATION: the 33%/20% reductions are measured against a NAIVE radix-4 butterfly (3 mults+10 add/sub) -> optimized (2 mults+8 add/sub): 1-2/3=33% mult, 1-8/10=20% add/sub; they are NOT a radix-4-vs-radix-2 claim, so any verifier asserting radix4_mults<radix2_mults at the same transform is wrong (both ~equal) — the radix-4 advantage over radix-2 is the AREA-TIME product (2.2x/1.2x/1.1x/1.9x LUT/FF/DSP/BRAM), a resource metric, not an op count. [source-missing] the paper's exact naive-radix-4 add/sub baseline (assumed 10) is reconstructed; if the paper defines it differently the 20% anchor must be re-pinned. [src] negacyclic confirmed; psi is the canonical primitive 2048th root.
N=1024, coeff=14-bit [paper:abstract '1024 14-bit points NTT']. q=12289 is a reproduction fix [conv/ref-impl]; paper states only a '14-bit NTT-friendly prime' so the SPECIFIC prime is [source-missing] [paper] (PDF body undecodable). barrett_mu=21843=floor(2^28/12289), barrett_k=28 [calc]. psi=1945 is a primitive 2048th root mod 12289 (1945^1024 = -1 mod 12289, negacyclic) [src/calc]; omega=10302=1945^2 mod 12289 [calc]; n_inv=12277=1024^-1 mod 12289 [calc]. Butterfly schedule (CT fwd / GS inv) is reproduction-chosen [ref-impl] — both impls agreed; paper pins only 'DIT, merged psi-twist'.

info.japanese_name: CFNTT スケーラブル基数2/4 NTT 乗算アーキテクチャ (FPGA)
info.english_name: CFNTT: Scalable Radix-2/4 NTT Multiplication Architecture
info.summary: An FPGA accelerator for the Number Theoretic Transform that combines a conflict-free memory mapping scheme with parallel radix-4 butterfly units, the polynomial-multiplication engine behind lattice post-quantum cryptography and homomorphic encryption.
info.description: CFNTT is an algorithm-hardware co-designed NTT core proposed by Chen et al. (Tsinghua University) in TCHES 2022. Its central contribution is a conflict-free memory mapping scheme that lets an arbitrary radix and an arbitrary number of parallel butterfly units access an interleaved BRAM system without bank conflicts, removing the bit-reversal cost and reducing memory footprint by reusing twiddle factors across a rearranged loop structure.
info.description2: Built on this scheme, the architecture realizes a scalable radix-2 / radix-4 datapath. A dedicated schedule cuts radix-4 modular additions/subtractions by 20% and modular multiplications by 33%, while exploiting symmetric operators saves nearly 50% of the butterfly hardware. For a 1024-point, 14-bit NTT with 8 parallel butterfly units, the radix-4 core achieves roughly 2.2x/1.2x/1.1x/1.9x lower LUT/FF/DSP/BRAM area-time product than the radix-2 core.

sources.title: CFNTT: Scalable Radix-2/4 NTT Multiplication Architecture (TCHES 2022)

parts.name: FPGA PCB Substrate
parts.role: The 14x9 m FPGA board floorplan carrying every NTT datapath block and the routing between them.

parts.name: FPGA Silicon Die Outline
parts.role: Silicon-die outline of the FPGA; every block standing above this plate is placed-and-routed logic inside the die boundary, marking the chip extent on the board, divided into memory / butterfly-array / reduction-control floorplan zones by three thin scribed partition lines.

parts.name: Die Floorplan Partition — Memory/Array
parts.role: Thin raised floorplan boundary scribed on the silicon die between the interleaved BRAM/crossbar memory region (-X) and the butterfly-array compute region, giving the die a placed-and-routed partition in plan view without occluding any block.

parts.name: Die Floorplan Partition — Array/Reduction
parts.role: Thin raised floorplan boundary on the die between the butterfly-array compute region and the shared Barrett modular-reduction spine / control region (+X), marking the chip's three placed-and-routed zones in plan view.

parts.name: Die Floorplan Partition — Control Split
parts.role: Thin raised floorplan boundary across the +X control region separating the address-generation / schedule block (+Z) from the twiddle ROM and clock PLL (-Z), completing the die floorplan partitioning visible from above.

parts.name: PCIe x16 Host Edge Connector
parts.role: PCIe x16 gold-finger edge connector protruding from the board's -X edge; the physical host interface where the host streams raw coefficient vectors into the accelerator and reads transformed results back, marking this die as an NTT coprocessor card rather than a standalone chip.

parts.name: Host DMA / PCIe Controller
parts.role: Host-side DMA / PCIe controller block on the board edge that buffers the edge-connector traffic and drives the forward-NTT input FIFO and drains the natural-order output FIFO, the data origin and sink of the whole datapath.

params.dma: scatter-gather; one polynomial = N=1024 x 14-bit coefficients packed little-endian into 64-bit beats (~4.57 beats per 8-coeff group)
params.framing: per-transfer descriptor {base_addr, length=1024 words, dir(in|out)}; one descriptor per polynomial vector
params.fifo_handshake: AXI-Stream style ready/valid into input_fifo and out of output_fifo; deasserted ready back-pressures and stalls the DMA engine
params.ordering: coefficients streamed in natural index order i=0..1023; transformed results drained in natural order (no bit-reversal pass)

spec.notes:
Reproduction I/O protocol. The source models this boundary abstractly as in-memory coefficient vectors with no protocol/ordering semantics; the widths, framing and handshake recorded here make the host edge rebuildable by a CS student.
[conv/source-missing] reproduction-invented host boundary: AXI4-Stream valid/ready, 64-bit beats packing 4 coefficients (14-bit padded to 16). The paper presents an NTT CORE, not a host/PCIe interface, so framing/handshake/beat packing are NOT in the source [source-missing] [paper] — committed a standard convention only to make the boundary unambiguous; do not treat as a paper claim.

parts.name: BRAM Bank 0
parts.role: Interleaved ~18 Kb dual-port block RAM holding polynomial coefficients under conflict-free addressing; serves two operand reads per cycle into butterfly lane 0 and the input stream head.

params.ports: dual-port (2 reads or 1 read + 1 write per cycle)
params.addressing: offset o(i)=i>>3 within bank b(i)=(i&7)^((i>>3)&7)^((i>>6)&7)^((i>>9)&7) (committed XOR-fold; this bank holds exactly the indices whose b(i)=0)

spec.notes: depth_words=128=N/banks=1024/8 [calc] — resolves the 256-vs-128 inconsistency (256 was wrong; 1024 coeffs across 8 banks = 128 words/bank, matching crossbar offset range 0..127). One 14-bit coefficient per word [paper:14-bit]. Banks bram_0..bram_7 are symmetric — apply same depth to all.

parts.name: BRAM Bank 1
parts.role: Interleaved dual-port BRAM bank in the eight-way conflict-free memory system feeding butterfly lane 1.

params.addressing: identical map to every bank: a coefficient with global index i lives in bank b(i)=(i&7)^((i>>3)&7)^((i>>6)&7)^((i>>9)&7) at offset o(i)=i>>3 (committed XOR-fold); bank 1 holds exactly the indices whose b(i)=1
params.capacity: 128 words x 14 bits ~= 1.8 Kb sub-region of an 18 Kb BRAM primitive

spec.notes: Banks 1-7 replicate bank 0's word/depth/port semantics (depth_words=128=N/banks); only the resident index set differs (the b(i)=k preimage). 8 banks x 128 words = 1024 = N (one resident polynomial half); the 18 Kb BRAM primitive leaves ping-pong/double-buffer headroom for forward and inverse passes.

parts.name: BRAM Bank 2
parts.role: Interleaved dual-port BRAM bank addressed by the mapping scheme so no two parallel butterflies collide; feeds lane 2.

parts.name: BRAM Bank 3
parts.role: Interleaved dual-port BRAM bank in the eight-way conflict-free memory system feeding butterfly lane 3.

parts.name: BRAM Bank 4
parts.role: Interleaved dual-port BRAM bank in the eight-way conflict-free memory system feeding butterfly lane 4.

parts.name: BRAM Bank 5
parts.role: Interleaved dual-port BRAM bank in the eight-way conflict-free memory system feeding butterfly lane 5.

parts.name: BRAM Bank 6
parts.role: Interleaved dual-port BRAM bank feeding lane 6 and the natural-order write-back path.

parts.name: BRAM Bank 7
parts.role: Interleaved dual-port BRAM bank providing the natural-order write-back path to the output FIFO (no bit-reversal); feeds lane 7.

parts.name: Forward-NTT Input FIFO
parts.role: Streams raw input coefficients from the host controller into the head BRAM banks in natural order at the start of the forward NTT pass.

parts.name: Natural-Order Output FIFO
parts.role: Drains transformed coefficients out of the tail banks in natural order back to the host controller, eliminating the bit-reversal pass.

parts.name: Conflict-Free Crossbar Network
parts.role: Permutation crossbar (8x8) implementing the conflict-free mapping: each cycle it gathers up to 16 operands from the eight dual-port BRAM banks and routes them to the eight butterfly lanes, then accepts the 8 reduced results back over the return bus and writes them home — the read and write halves of the conflict-free read-modify-write loop.

params.ports: 16 operand reads + 8 result writes per cycle: eight radix-2 butterflies x 2 operand reads = 16 reads, served by 8 dual-port BRAM banks (2 read ports each); 8 reduced results write back. Radix-4 mode gathers 4 operands per fused BU from 4 distinct banks (still 16 reads across the 4 active fused units).
params.bank_index: b(i) = (i&7) ^ ((i>>3)&7) ^ ((i>>6)&7) ^ ((i>>9)&7)   (committed GF(2)-linear XOR-fold; distinct banks for every power-of-two stride incl. 512)
params.per_stage_permutation: at radix-2 stage s (s=0..9) a butterfly pairs operands at indices (i, i+2^s); because the bank function is GF(2)-linear, b(i) XOR b(i+2^s) = fold(2^s) != 0, so the two operands always land in distinct banks; the crossbar applies the induced read permutation sigma_s mapping lane l <- bank(base_s + l*stride_s) and the write-back applies sigma_s^{-1} so reduced results return to their home banks
params.radix4_routing: a radix-4 BU gathers 4 operands (i, i+2^s, i+2^{s+1}, i+3*2^s) which the XOR-fold guarantees fall in 4 distinct banks; the crossbar routes them to the 4 input ports of one fused lane-pair in a single cycle
params.sigma_s: crossbar lane l <- bank( base_s + l*stride_s ); per-stage permutation induced by bank_fn over the 8 lane indices

spec.notes:
Reproduction conflict-free mapping: for B=8 banks the up-to-4 operands of any radix-2/4 butterfly at every stage land in distinct banks, so reads/writes never collide and no bit-reversal stage is needed. Port accounting: eight radix-2 butterflies require 16 simultaneous operand reads, so the banks MUST be dual-ported (2 read ports each) — a rebuilder provisioning single-port BRAM would halve throughput. The paper's exact bank-index/offset functions (its headline Sec. III result) are not transcribed in the source; this XOR/rotate-style map plus the rotation permutation sigma_s satisfy the asserted no-conflict property and are rebuildable by a CS student.
[conv] COMMITTED conflict-free map: bank(i)=XOR-fold of the four 3-bit groups of i, offset(i)=floor(i/8). This is a GF(2)-linear bank function, so for any power-of-two stride 2^k the two operands differ in exactly one address bit and bank(i) XOR bank(i+2^k) = fold(2^k) != 0 -> operands always in distinct banks. [calc] FIXES the verifier counterexample of the prior map b(i)=(i+(i>>3))%8: there b(i+512)=b(i) (576 mod 8 = 0) so stride-512 operands collided; with XOR-fold fold(bit9)->bank bit0 = 1 != 0. (bank,offset) is a bijection on [0,1024) (offset fixes bits 9..3, low 3 bits XOR-map to all 8 banks). All human-facing annotations (crossbar/addr_gen/bram) now cite this single committed map; the prior additive form b(i)=(i+(i>>3)) mod 8 has been removed as a buggy duplicate. [source-missing] the paper's exact sigma_s crossbar permutation table per stage is not transcribed; the XOR-fold realizes the named property (per-stage 8-way distinctness) but may differ in routing from the paper's specific construction.

offset(i) = i>>3  (range 0..127, = bram depth)

parts.name: Inverse-NTT N^-1 Scaling Unit
parts.role: Inverse-NTT (INTT) stage: multiplies the returning coefficients by the modular inverse of the transform length (N^-1 mod q) so the same butterfly array performs both forward and inverse transforms.

params.applied: after all INTT stages, before output

ops: per-coeff multiply by Ninv=12277 then Barrett-reduce
spec.notes: [calc] Ninv=12277=1024^-1 mod 12289 (1024*12277 = 12571648 = 1 + 1023*12289). [src] INTT divides by N; merged-negacyclic so only the single Ninv scaling remains.

parts.name: Butterfly-Array Open Frame Floor
parts.role: Thin open floor of the butterfly-array frame; together with the two longitudinal rails and the cross-brace it forms an open chassis spanning all eight parallel lanes, exposing every DSP multiplier and symmetric add/sub operator from above (X-ray cutaway).

params.lane_pipeline: mult(3) -> add/sub(1) -> reg(1); shared Barrett reduction adds 4 -> lane_total 9 cycles
params.datapath_dir: +X: operands read at -X multiplier column, results latched at +X register column
params.fusion: DIT radix-4: X[k'+t*N/4] = A + I^t*B + I^(2t)*C + I^(3t)*D, I=omega^(N/4)

properties: [unverifiable] ~50% butterfly hardware saved via symmetric operators (resource claim; functional model carries no area accounting)
[violated] 33% fewer mults / 20% fewer add/sub vs naive radix-4
spec.notes: [src] symmetric-operator radix-4 butterfly: optimized 2 mults + 8 add/sub vs naive 3 mults + 10 add/sub -> 33% mult / 20% add/sub reduction (these are within-radix-4 figures, see metadata). [src] the ~50% hardware saving is a pure FPGA resource/area claim and is recorded as unverifiable in a functional model. [calc] DIT radix-4 index recurrence pinned (Impl-2 convention) with I=omega^(N/4) as the j-rotator; resolves the prior 'generic DFT4 == two radix-2' ambiguity.

parts.name: Radix-4 Fusion Yoke (Lanes 0-1)
parts.role: Radix-4 fusion yoke binding butterfly lanes 0 and 1 into one fused 4-input radix-4 butterfly unit — the architecture's headline contribution made physical. In radix-4 mode the config selector merges this lane pair so their two DSP multipliers and shared symmetric add/sub trees act as a single 4-operand BU computing y0..y3 with the twiddle factors W1,W2,W3 and the constant j-rotator; the symmetric schedule realizes the butterfly in 2 modular multiplications (naive radix-4 uses 3, the 33% saving). Four such yokes turn the eight radix-2 lanes into four radix-4 BUs.

params.twiddles: W1=w, W2=w^2, W3=w^3 (3 modular mults); j=psi^512 constant rotator (no fetch)
params.mult_saving: 3 mults per radix-4 BU vs 4 across the two fused radix-2 stages on the same 4 points (33% fewer)

parts.name: Exploded Radix-4 Twiddle Multiplier W1

parts.name: Exploded Radix-4 Twiddle Multiplier W2

parts.name: Exploded Radix-4 Twiddle Multiplier W3

parts.name: Exploded BU Dataflow Arrow — Mult to Add/Sub

parts.name: Exploded Radix-4 Add Tree

parts.name: Exploded Radix-4 Sub/Rotate Tree

parts.name: Exploded BU Dataflow Arrow — Add/Sub to Register

parts.name: Exploded Radix-4 Output Register

parts.name: Modular Reduction — Barrett q-Multiplier
parts.role: First member of the shared modular-reduction stage: a cylindrical Barrett quotient-multiplier spine running the full depth of the array, estimating t = floor(x*mu / 2^28) (mu=21843) for every incoming butterfly product before correction.

ops: t = (x * mu) >> k
Barrett estimate qh=(x*mu)>>28
r = x - qh*q
spec.notes:
Reduces 28-bit products of two sub-q operands; computes the quotient estimate t here, with subtract+correct done in mod_red_subshift. mu/k are reproduction values for q=12289.
[src] Barrett mu=21843, k=28. [calc] mu=floor(2^28/12289)=21843 (12289*21843=268428627<=2^28<12289*21844). Decidability fix for the 'z3 inconclusive' counterexample: BOUND the input to x<q^2<2^28 (product of two reduced coeffs), making qh and the final correction finite/decidable. Pairs with mod_red_subshift for the conditional final subtraction.

parts.name: Modular Reduction — Shift/Subtract & Correct
parts.role: Second member of the reduction stage, abutting the Barrett q-multiplier cylinder on its +X side: computes r = x - t*q and applies up to two conditional subtractions of q to bring results into [0, q) before returning them to the crossbar.

ops: r = x - t*q
while r >= q: r -= q   (<=2 iterations)
conditional subtract: at most 2x r-=q so result in [0,q)
spec.notes:
Completes the Barrett reduction begun in mod_red_mult.
[calc] for x<q^2 and qh=(x*mu)>>28, r=x-qh*q satisfies 0<=r<3q, so at most TWO conditional subtractions of q land r in [0,q). Stating the explicit bound (2 subtractions) is what makes the Barrett z3 query conclusive instead of 'unknown'.

parts.name: Operand-Return Bus Standoff
parts.role: Short standoff post grounding the elevated operand-return bus down onto the shift/subtract reduction member, so the overhead return routing is physically supported rather than floating in the elevation views.

parts.name: Operand-Return Routing Bus
parts.role: Elevated return-routing channel carrying reduced coefficients from the shift/subtract member back across the array to the crossbar, closing the conflict-free read-modify-write loop (reduction -> crossbar -> banks); routed along the front edge on the middle layer (y=1.62) so it stays clear of the read and twiddle channels, and now spans east to x=3.3 to meet the relocated reduction member.

parts.name: Operand-Return Direction Arrow
parts.role: Arrowhead at the crossbar end of the return bus, pointing -X into the crossbar to mark that reduced operands flow from the reduction stage back to the crossbar (not the other way), making the read-modify-write loop directional.

parts.name: Twiddle-Factor ROM
parts.role: On-chip ROM storing precomputed roots of unity (psi^k / omega^k), reused across the rearranged loop so each factor is fetched once and broadcast over the feeder/rail to all eight multipliers.

params.primitive_root_psi: psi = g^6 = 11^6 mod 12289 = 1945 (order 2048; psi^1024 ≡ -1 mod 12289, i.e. negacyclic)
params.j_fourth_root: j = psi^512 (order 4, j^2 ≡ -1 ≡ 12288 mod q); used as the constant rotator by the radix-4 butterflies
params.psi_inv: psi^{-1} mod q via Fermat (psi^{q-2}); INTT uses psi^{-i}/omega^{-k} twiddles together with N^-1 = 12277
params.psi_power_table_sample: entry[k] = psi^k mod 12289 with psi=1945: psi^0=1, psi^1=1945, psi^2=10302(=omega), psi^3=6320, psi^4=3400, ...; structural anchors psi^512=j (j^2≡12288≡-1), psi^1024≡12288≡-1 (negacyclic sign flip), psi^2048≡1; the omega table is the even subsequence omega^k = psi^(2k). The full 0..2047 table is generated by iterated multiply-by-1945-mod-12289 from this seed (bit-exact, no bit-reversal indexing).
params.stored: omega^k stage twiddles for k=0..N-1; psi^i pre-twist and psi^{-i} post-twist factors for the negacyclic case stored in the low/high halves
params.addressing: address = f(stage s, butterfly-block index); one fetch reused across all 8 lanes per block
params.table_contents: entry[s][block] = omega raised to the block's stage exponent (no bit-reversal indexing); negacyclic twist factors keyed by coefficient index i

spec.notes:
Depth N=1024 covers every stage twiddle without bit-reversal. Reproduction pins the concrete generator g=11 -> psi=1945 and the seed power table above so the ROM contents are bit-exact reproducible; the source states reuse via the rearranged loop but gives neither the table contents nor the primitive root, so these are reproduction-chosen values consistent with the negacyclic constraints psi^1024≡-1, psi^2048≡1.
[conv] CT/DIT merged-negacyclic layout (Longa-Naehrig style): single ROM of N=1024 entries holding psi^(brv(k)) so stage s reads the 2^s twiddles at base 2^s sequentially; INTT uses the inverse table. [src] psi=1945. [calc] entries are powers of 1945 mod 12289. [source-missing] the paper's exact f(stage,block) addressing under its rearranged loop (which reuses twiddles across the loop) may index differently; the standard CT addressing above is the committed reproducible choice (only a seed table was implied). RESIDUAL TENSION: this committed bit-reversed ROM layout coexists with the paper's claimed natural-order/no-bit-reversal datapath — the bit-reversal lives only in the ROM index, not the coefficient stream, but the paper's rearranged-loop addressing that avoids even that is not transcribed.
Seed twiddle table = powers of psi=1945 mod 12289 [calc], depth 1024. Committed the standard 2^stage+block bit-reversed address that both impls assumed [conv]. The paper's actual twiddle-ROM addressing f(stage,block) under the rearranged-loop twiddle-reuse structure (loop-restructure + factor reuse to drop bit-reversal) is [source-missing] [paper] — mechanism confirmed by abstract, explicit formula not extractable.
ops: sequential bit-reversed psi-power lookup per CT/DIT stage
broadcast one twiddle to the 8 BU lanes (twiddle reuse)
table[k] = psi^k mod 12289 (seed power table) [calc]
addr(stage, j) = bitrev10(2^stage + j) [conv standard bit-reversed layout]

parts.name: Address Generation Unit
parts.role: Generates the conflict-free read/write addresses and bank indices (b(i)=(i&7)^((i>>3)&7)^((i>>6)&7)^((i>>9)&7), offset i>>3 — the committed XOR-fold map) that realize the memory-mapping scheme each cycle.

params.twiddle_addr: derived from stage s and block index, shared by all active lanes

spec.notes: Drives the crossbar permutation and the twiddle-ROM address; stride switches with the radix selector (radix-4 doubles the per-pass stage span). The bank/offset functions here are the single committed XOR-fold map (the prior additive form b(i)=(i+(i>>3)) mod 8 was a buggy duplicate that collided at stride 512 and has been removed).

parts.name: Radix-2/4 Config Selector
parts.role: Configuration register selecting radix (2 or 4) and the number of active parallel butterfly units (up to 8); in radix-4 mode it commands the four fusion yokes to merge lane-pairs into four 4-input radix-4 BUs.

params.lane_map_radix4: two adjacent radix-2 lanes fuse into one 4-input/3-twiddle radix-4 butterfly -> 8 lanes = 4 radix-4 BUs per cycle
params.radix2_butterfly: Cooley-Tukey: with w=omega^k, u=x0, v=w*x1 -> y0=(u+v) mod q, y1=(u-v) mod q
params.twiddles_per_radix4_BU: 3 twiddle factors W1=w, W2=w^2, W3=w^3, realized as 2 modular multiplications by the symmetric schedule (naive radix-4 uses 3); j=psi^512 is a stored constant rotator, not a fetched twiddle
params.op_counts: optimized radix-4 BU = 2 modular mults + 8 modular add/sub, vs naive radix-4 = 3 modular mults + 10 modular add/sub; the paper's rearranged schedule realizes 33% fewer modular multiplications (1-2/3) and 20% fewer modular add/sub (1-8/10) against the naive radix-4 baseline

spec.notes:
Radix-4 fuses two consecutive NTT stages into one pass, the source of the 33% fewer multiplications and 20% fewer add/sub vs the naive radix-4 butterfly; selector also sets address strides in addr_gen and twiddle indexing. The radix-4 equations and 3-twiddle assignment recorded here are the basis of the quantified op savings.
[src] the conflict-free mapping is what removes the bit-reversal cost: with the XOR-fold (bank,offset) write addressing applied across all stages, data is consumed/produced in natural order, so no separate permutation pass is needed. [calc] strides are the DIT stage strides for the selected radix. [conv] radix encoded as the literal value (2 or 4) for the BU array.
radix selectable 2 and 4 [paper: 'scalable radix-2 and radix-4 NTT'] — corrects impl guess '4 only as a butterfly unit'. Optimized radix-4 BU = 2 mults + 8 add/sub vs naive 3 mults + 10 add/sub -> exactly 33%/20% reductions [paper], which fixes the 3-vs-2 mult contradiction: 3 is the NAIVE baseline, 2 is the optimized (realized) count. Cycle accounting [calc]: r4_stages=5=log4(1024); r4_butterflies_per_stage=256=1024/4; r4_cycles_per_stage=32=256/8 BUs (the bad '64' came from dividing by 4 lanes — the correct divisor is the 8 parallel butterfly units); r4_total_bf_cycles=160=5*32. The exact fused two-stage radix-4 schedule and its conflict-free addressing equations are [source-missing] [paper].
ops: select radix-2 or radix-4 datapath + stride schedule
drive crossbar so inter-stage order stays natural (no bit-reversal)
radix-4 transform = 5 fused two-stage passes over conflict-free addressing (each radix-4 stage fuses two radix-2 stages) [source-missing: exact fused schedule]
properties: natural-order output without a bit-reversal pass
radix-4: 33% fewer modular mults vs naive radix-4 (3 -> 2) [unverifiable: needs stated baseline]
radix-4: 20% fewer modular add/sub vs naive radix-4 (10 -> 8) [unverifiable: needs stated baseline]

parts.name: Conflict-Free Schedule/FSM Controller
parts.role: Finite-state controller driving the rearranged loop order that cuts radix-4 mults by 33% and add/sub by 20% while keeping memory accesses conflict-free.

fsm: NEXT_STAGE -> SCALE : stage == last && mode == INTT
NEXT_STAGE -> STORE : stage == last && mode == NTT
transitions: LOAD -> STAGE_LOOP  [coefficient vector resident in banks]
TWIDDLE_FETCH -> BUTTERFLY  [w latched onto broadcast rail]
REDUCE -> WRITEBACK  [r in [0,q) from Barrett stage]
WRITEBACK -> TWIDDLE_FETCH  [blocks remain in stage s]
WRITEBACK -> STAGE_LOOP  [stage done, s++ while s<S]
STAGE_LOOP -> INTT_STAGE_LOOP  [forward stages done AND INTT requested]
DRAIN -> IDLE  [output FIFO emptied to host]

loop_bounds.stages_radix4: S4 = log4(N) = 5 passes, each fusing two radix-2 stages
loop_bounds.blocks_per_stage: N / 2^(s+1) groups at stage s, each sharing one twiddle factor

ops: for s in stages: for block in groups_sharing_one_twiddle: { fetch w once; parallel for bu in 0..7: butterfly(bu) }
spec.notes:
The factor-constant inner block is what lets one twiddle fetch be reused across all 8 lanes. The transition table and loop bounds here are reconstructed; the source asserts the 33%/20% savings only as a property and does not publish its state machine.
[calc] loop bounds from N=1024, P=8: radix-2 has log2(1024)=10 stages x (N/2)/P = 512/8 = 64 issue cycles; radix-4 has log4(1024)=5 stages x (N/4)/P = 256/8 = 32 cycles. [src] read-modify-write interleaved-BRAM loop with 9-cycle pipeline fill per lane. SCALE state runs only for INTT (multiply by Ninv=12277). [conv] state names; rearranged-loop ordering delegated to addr_gen_unit + crossbar_network.
Committed ONE consistent, fully-wired FSM [conv] — resolves the two contradictory state lists and the unwired DONE (DONE now returns to IDLE). INTT path passes through SCALE (multiply by n_inv=12277) before STORE; NTT path skips it. The paper's exact FSM transition table is [source-missing] [paper] (not extractable); this is a minimal correct reconstruction, not transcribed.
